```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from IPython.display import HTML, Image
from scipy.special import airy
```

## Drawing Lines

```{python}
x = np.linspace(-np.pi, np.pi)
y = np.cos(x)
plt.plot(x, y)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
x = np.linspace(-np.pi, np.pi)
y = np.cos(x)
plt.plot(x, y, "g--")  
plt.xlabel("x")
plt.ylabel("y")
plt.title("cos(x)")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
x = np.linspace(-np.pi, np.pi)
y = np.cos(x)
# Here a string from 0->1 specifies a gray value.
plt.plot(x, y, "-", color="0.15")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
x = np.linspace(-np.pi, np.pi)
y = np.cos(x)
plt.plot(x, y, "--", color="#FD8706")  # We can also use hex colors if we want.
plt.show()
```

```{python}
x = np.linspace(-np.pi, np.pi)
y = np.cos(x)
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 3))  # This controls the size of the figure
plt.subplot(2, 3, 1)  # This is the first plot in a 2x3 grid of plots
plt.plot(x, y)
plt.subplot(2, 3, 2)  # this is the second plot
plt.plot(x, y, linestyle="-")  # Demo using 'linestyle' keyword arguement
plt.subplot(2, 3, 3)
plt.plot(x, y, ".")
plt.subplot(2, 3, 4)
plt.plot(x, y, "-.")
plt.subplot(2, 3, 5)
plt.plot(x, y, ".-")
plt.subplot(2, 3, 6)
plt.plot(x, y, ls=":")  # Demo using 'ls' keyword arguement.
plt.show()
```

```{python}
x = np.linspace(0, 10)
y = np.exp(x)
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 3))
plt.subplot(1, 3, 1)
plt.plot(x, y)
plt.subplot(1, 3, 2)
plt.plot(x, y, linewidth=6)
plt.subplot(1, 3, 3)
plt.plot(x, y, lw=3.75)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
x = np.linspace(0, 10)
s = np.sin(x)
c = np.cos(x)
sx = x * np.cos(x)
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 3))
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
# call three different plot functions
plt.plot(x, s, "b")
plt.plot(x, c, "r")
plt.plot(x, sx, "g")
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
# combine multiple lines in one call to plot
plt.plot(x, s, "b", x, c, "r", x, sx, "g")
plt.show()
```

## Setting Axes Limits

```{python}
x = np.linspace(-np.pi, np.pi, 100)
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 3))
plt.subplot(1, 3, 1)
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x), lw=2)
plt.subplot(1, 3, 2)
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x), lw=2, color="#750005")
plt.xlim([-np.pi, np.pi])  # change bounds on x-axis to [-pi,pi]
plt.subplot(1, 3, 3)
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x), "^", ms=3, color="0.9")
plt.xlim([-1, 1])  # change bounds on x-axis to [-1,1]
plt.ylim([-0.75, 1.75])  # change bounds on y-axis to [-0.75,0.75]
plt.show()
```

## Saving Figures

```{python}
x = np.linspace(-np.pi, np.pi, 100)
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 3))
plt.subplot(1, 3, 1)
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x), lw=2)
plt.subplot(1, 3, 2)
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x), lw=2, color="#640007")
plt.xlim([-np.pi, np.pi])
plt.subplot(1, 3, 3)
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x), "^", ms=5, color="0.1")
plt.xlim([-1, 1])
plt.ylim([-0.75, 1.75])
plt.savefig(
    "axes_example.png"
)
```

## Using Shapes for Data Points

```{python}
x = np.linspace(-1, 1)
Ai, Aip, Bi, Bip = airy(x)
plt.plot(x, Ai, "b*", x, Aip, "ro", x, Bi, "gs", x, Bip, "k-")
plt.show()
```

## Other Kinds of 2D Plots

```{python}
x = np.linspace(-1, 1.0, 100)
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 6))
plt.subplot(2, 2, 1)
y = x + 0.25 * np.random.randn(len(x))
plt.scatter(x, y, color="m")  # plot collection of (x,y) points
plt.title("A scatter Plot")
plt.subplot(2, 2, 2)
n = np.array([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
plt.bar(
    n, n**2, align="center", width=1
)  # aligns the bars over the x-numbers, and width=dx
plt.title("A bar Plot")
plt.subplot(2, 2, 3)
plt.fill_between(
    x, x**2, x**3, color="green"
)  # fill between x**2 & x**3 with green
plt.title("A fill_between Plot")
plt.subplot(2, 2, 4)
plt.title("A hist Plot")
r = np.random.randn(50)  # generating some random numbers
plt.hist(r, color="y")  # create a histogram of the random number values
plt.show()
```
